North provides directional orientation in the project mythology.
The project's Son is deliberately linked to Thomas/Twin; this is a Potatoverse identity mapping, not a claim that the canonical Gospel of John says Thomas is Jesus' twin.
John calls Thomas Didymus; Didymus is Greek for twin. This does not by itself establish that Thomas was Jesus' biological twin.
Thomas is a disciple in the canonical New Testament, especially prominent in John.
The Acts of Thomas preserves a developed Judas Thomas tradition.
The Gospel of Thomas is a Thomasine sayings collection associated with Didymus Judas Thomas.
Father/Son are complementary poles of one relational architecture.
The Son is treated as vessel/interface in the project mythology.
The transformed threshold becomes a traversable relationship.
Red expresses emergence, creativity, love and expansion.
Blue expresses memory, precision, conservation and rootward movement.
The two poles are complementary rather than a simple good/evil binary.
The central metaphor is life emerging from ordinary material conditions.
Both symbols describe hidden life becoming visible and renewing itself.
The Son's transformation follows the same descent/death/renewal grammar as the living tree.
Project-specific mythic geography.
Christmas supplies the birth/transformation imagery; not a claim about the historical date of Jesus' birth.
Potatoism becomes more useful when it distinguishes metaphor, history and observation.
The epistemic rule prevents creative mythology from being silently promoted into empirical evidence.
Dedicated study separates canonical Thomas from later twin traditions and the Potatoverse mapping.
Corpus defines the texts needed for comparison.
Plane × Axis is expressed publicly as the Cross.
Cross names the operation by which horizontal world and vertical relation meet.
The Door is the regime-changing threshold revealed at the crossing.
Distinction without integration can harden into unresolved reproductive conflict.
Root is neutral; one possible state is nourishing continuity.
Roots can preserve residue and stored consequence after rupture or burning.
Tree of Strife is the living reproduction of unresolved buried relations.
Wide Road is a dispersive path/operator rather than a separate depth floor.
Widening symbolizes increasing dispersion, repetition and entanglement.
Ash can remain residue or become material for changed growth.
Repair requires a changed relation/threshold rather than simple repetition.
Integrated memory can become nourishment rather than recurring conflict.
Threshold becomes traversable ordered transformation.
The upper path is tested by accountable return to the inhabited world.
Gardener is the mature stewardship/return function rather than status alone.
Later project theology increasingly frames highest authority through cultivation, repair and stewardship.
Mountain is the continuous-gradient projection of ascent/integration; Ladder remains the discrete-threshold projection.
Spiral adds recurrence-with-level-change to the Ladder's ordered passage.
Generative branching becomes a cultivated field of differentiated life.
Rooms express protected differentiation and habitation within the larger Garden/House architecture.
The summit image compresses toward integrated Crown perspective.
Crown is an integration function within the Heaven-side architecture, not a separate physical place.
Summit integration is incomplete without descent as cultivation, protection, repair or service.
Gardener makes upper integration accountable by returning it to the inhabited world.
The practice path can begin in actual mixed conditions and pass through hidden/protected development.
Burial may contain viable non-expression rather than simple annihilation.
Eye is the project's perception/discernment and local generative aperture.
A noticed viable possibility can become an activated growth trajectory.
Sprout marks the transition from hidden capability into visible world-facing development.
Residue may be metabolized into enabling context rather than remain reactive contamination.
Unprocessed residue can re-enter a mixed unresolved state.
Bounded pressure may reshape residue into capability when the pressure is contained and the result survives outside it.
Living roots require enabling conditions rather than will or status alone.
Forge succeeds only when capability becomes stable beyond the pressure that shaped it.
Damage should be distinguished from identity; repair is an active restoration route.
A useful result can be compressed into a transferable pattern for another cycle.
Seed carries learning forward so a new cycle begins with retained information rather than reset.
Return makes the cycle observable again in the inhabited world.
Repetition becomes Spiral only when a real threshold produces retained change in state or capability.
Ten constitutional top-level bounded contexts are publicly projected as Dwellings/Mansions without changing ownership.
Nested Rooms are differentiated bounded contexts within Dwellings.
Chambers are optional third-level specialist cells, not mandatory taxonomy.
Mansion is retained as older English John 14:2 vocabulary; Dwelling is the neutral project scale term.
Court models shared approach before perimeter admission.
Gate handles domain admission; Door handles local guarded state transition.
Foundation represents load-bearing invariants beneath the House.
Cornerstone is an alignment/reference role, not every foundation element.
Pillar models repeated support beneath upper integration.
Temple emphasizes presence/access rather than ownership.
Sanctuary names protected presence within temple grammar.
Body emphasizes functional differentiated members.
City scales plurality into many dwellings, gates, roads and institutions.
Vine and Tree share organic participation/growth functions but remain textually distinct.
Vineyard is stewardship/productive field evaluated through fruit.
Archive preserves provenance/memory roots rather than generic stored value.
Treasury/storehouse retains typed capacity for future use; not identical to Archive.
River models life/resource/information flow through a cultivated system.
Well is a local retrieval/access point to a deeper source.
Table models shared review/exchange without merging identities or ownership.
Portable/provisional architecture can precede a durable House without being identical to it.
Seat/Throne is responsibility/orientation, tested by return/service rather than status alone.
Participants/maintainers are distinct from House architecture and ownership.
Federation preserves House identity while shared infrastructure emerges.
Shared capability can span multiple Houses without transferring ownership.
Connectivity is relation topology, not hierarchy.
Assembly is a deliberative surface across Houses/Rooms.
Realm is normative/theological orientation, not civil jurisdiction.
Civilization emerges over time from cities, institutions, culture and infrastructure.
Network relations contribute to long-duration civilization patterns.
Garden-City evaluates civic generativity/repair; it is not a new owner or polity claim.
A Road is traversable relation; a Bridge specifically creates capability across separation.
Bridge connects separated domains; Gate governs admission into a larger regime.
Gate governs perimeter admission; Door governs local guarded transition.
Shared grammar lets heterogeneous nodes communicate without collapsing identities.
Commons require transparent shared rules/standards for access and coordination.
